claims.text: The feedstock is a pre-alloyed, free-flowing, cobalt-free AlCrFeNiSi high-entropy-alloy powder.
SPS at approximately 1100°C, 50 MPa, a heating rate of approximately 100°C/min, and a 5-minute dwell will produce a highly refined microstructure.
The specified SPS treatment will produce a nearly fully dense AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
The specified SPS treatment will minimize elemental segregation in AlCrFeNiSi.
The specified SPS treatment will reduce residual stress and defect formation relative to conventional bulk fabrication.
Rapid heating and a short dwell restrict diffusion and therefore limit compositional segregation.
Applying 50 MPa pressure during SPS accelerates densification.
Applying pressure during SPS promotes pore elimination.
Rapid cooling minimizes the onset of residual thermal stresses.
Rapid cooling avoids grain coarsening and other defect formation.
Improved microstructural homogeneity will increase the strength of SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventionally fabricated material.
Improved microstructural homogeneity will increase the ductility of SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventionally fabricated material.
Conventional bulk fabrication of AlCrFeNiSi typically uses slower heating and cooling cycles that permit elemental segregation.
Prolonged exposure to high temperature during conventional fabrication leads to residual stresses.
Conventional bulk fabrication has a greater likelihood of porosity and defect formation than the proposed SPS process.
